summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income certain income that insurance companies earn from providing real property insurance in federally declared disaster areas for five years following the disaster.

scores.thoughts: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude certain income from gross income for insurance companies providing real property insurance after federally declared disasters. This exclusion effectively lowers the tax burden for these specific companies, thus reducing tax revenue.

The bill creates a new tax exclusion for certain insurance company income in federally declared disaster areas, directly reducing federal tax revenue. Because the entire legislation consists of this revenue-losing provision, it has a clear, central effect of increasing the deficit to subsidize post-disaster insurance availability.
